The informal estimate during the incident was “maybe around 20 customers affected” from Chloe’s quick database check and Raj’s agreement of “about 20 customer environments” [NL-022-S03]. The official postmortem database audit later confirmed exactly 17 customer workspaces were directly affected by the upload pipeline and indexing queue outage [NL-022-S03]. That postmortem audit is the sole authority for customer-impact metrics, so the final impact is 17 customer workspaces, superseding the informal ~20 estimate [NL-013-S09].

The corrective work that addresses recurrence includes:

- An immediate retry cap: background workers now enforce a maximum of 5 retries with exponential backoff and randomized jitter (completed March 15, 2026) [NL-013-S07].
- A schema migration policy requiring multi-stage, lock-free migrations for large tables (completed March 16, 2026) [NL-013-S07].
- Granular Redis queue monitoring alerts for retry frequencies and worker connection states [NL-013-S07].
- Ingestion load testing under connection-starvation scenarios to verify the retry cap holds [NL-013-S07].
- Database pool isolation, separating write-heavy background tasks from read-heavy user query interfaces using a dedicated pgBouncer pool [NL-013-S07].
- SRE runbook revisions covering Redis queue backups, manual connection purging, read-only failovers, quarterly disaster recovery drills, and alerting validation within 120 seconds [NL-013-S09].
